---
title: "Filter and retrieve checklist records"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to the `funga_records()` function of the `fungaR` package. Unlike `funga_search()` and `funga_match()`, which resolve a list of names *you already have* against the checklist, `funga_records()` browses and filters the fungal side of the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) checklist directly — no input name list required.

## Function Overview

`funga_records()` downloads and parses the FFB dataset automatically (like `funga_search()`, reusing the local cache on repeated calls), then applies whichever combination of taxonomic, geographic, and trait-based filters you request. All filters are combined with a logical AND, and the result always has one row per matching taxon — appended with that taxon's distribution and species-profile information (see Output columns below).

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon` | Character vector. One or more family, genus, or species names to filter by (e.g. `c("Hymenochaetaceae", "Trichoderma", "Xylaria hypoxylon")`). |
| `taxonRank` | Character vector. Taxonomic rank(s) to keep (e.g. `"ESPECIE"`, `"VARIEDADE"`, `"SUBESPECIE"`, `"FORMA"`, `"GENERO"`, `"ORDEM"`, `"DIVISAO"` — fungi are classified by Division/phylum rather than Class). |
| `taxonomicStatus` | Character vector. FFB taxonomic status: `"NOME_ACEITO"` (accepted), `"SINONIMO"` (synonym), or `"NOME_DUVIDOSO"` (doubtful). |
| `state` | Character vector. Brazilian state(s), full name or acronym, diacritics-insensitive (e.g. `"Bahia"` or `"BA"`). |
| `phytogeographicDomain` | Character vector. Phytogeographic domain(s) (e.g. `"Caatinga"`, `"Mata Atlantica"`). |
| `endemism` | `TRUE`, `FALSE`, `"Brazil"`, or `NULL`. See [Endemism](#endemism) below. |
| `establishmentMeans` | Character vector. The taxon's origin in Brazil: `"native"`/`"nativa"` or `"introduced"`/`"exotic"`/`"exotica"` (English or Portuguese, case- and accent-insensitive). |
| `lifeForm`, `habitat`, `vegetationType` | Character vectors. Nutritional/ecological mode (e.g. `"Saprobio"`, `"Liquenizado"`), substrate/host (e.g. `"Tronco em decomposicao"`, `"Solo"`, `"Outro fungo"` — this is what `habitat` means for fungi, since FFB has no separate named host-taxon field) and vegetation type (e.g. `"Cerrado (lato sensu)"`). |
| `version` | Character. FFB dataset version to use. Defaults to `"latest"`. |
| `rm_funga_database` | Logical. If `TRUE`, deletes the downloaded database after the search. Default `FALSE` keeps it cached for faster repeated queries. |
| `verbose` | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |
| `save` | Logical. If `TRUE`, writes the filtered records to a CSV file. |
| `dir`, `filename` | Where and under what name to save the CSV when `save = TRUE`. |

## Output columns

Beyond the taxon table columns (`taxonName`, `family`, `genus`, `taxonRank`, `taxonomicStatus`, ...), every result also carries the matching taxon's distribution and species-profile information:

| Column | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | distribution table | Brazilian state(s) with occurrence records |
| `phytogeographicDomain` | distribution table | Phytogeographic domain(s) |
| `endemism` | distribution table | Endemism status as recorded by FFB |
| `establishmentMeans` | distribution table | Origin (native/introduced) as recorded by FFB |
| `lifeForm` | species profile table | Nutritional/ecological mode(s) |
| `habitat` | species profile table | Substrate/host record(s) |
| `vegetationType` | species profile table | Vegetation type(s) |

A single taxon can have several distribution or species-profile records (e.g. occurring in multiple states, or recorded on multiple substrates). Rather than multiplying rows, `funga_records()` concatenates all distinct values for each of these columns with `" | "`, so the result always keeps exactly one row per taxon — this happens regardless of which filters you applied, so even a taxon-only query returns its full distribution and species profile alongside it.

## Endemism

FFB's own `endemism` flag means **endemic to Brazil**. How `endemism` behaves therefore depends on whether you also give an area filter — `state`, `phytogeographicDomain`, or `vegetationType`:

- `endemism = TRUE` **without** an area filter returns every Brazilian endemic.
- `endemism = TRUE` **with** an area filter narrows further, to endemics *exclusive* to that area — taxa whose entire FFB range lies within it. `state = "Bahia", endemism = TRUE` returns taxa found only in Bahia, not every Brazilian endemic that merely also occurs there. Several values of one filter define a single combined area (`state = c("BA", "PE")`: taxa restricted to Bahia and/or Pernambuco), and combining several area filters requires exclusivity to each one.
- `endemism = "Brazil"` keeps Brazilian endemics that *occur* in the requested area(s), wherever else in Brazil they also occur — this is the "endemic AND occurring here" behavior you might expect from `TRUE` at first glance.
- `endemism = FALSE` is the complement of `TRUE`: non-endemics overall, or (with an area filter) taxa occurring there that are *not* exclusive to it.

```r
# Species endemic to Brazil overall
brazil_endemics <- funga_records(endemism = TRUE)

# Species endemic to Bahia specifically: found only in Bahia
bahia_endemics <- funga_records(state = "Bahia", endemism = TRUE)

# Brazilian endemics that occur in Bahia (and possibly elsewhere too)
brazil_endemics_in_bahia <- funga_records(state = "Bahia", endemism = "Brazil")
```

## Browse a whole family

```r
library(fungaR)

hymeno <- funga_records(taxon = "Hymenochaetaceae",
                        taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

## Filter by state and endemism

```r
bahia_endemics <- funga_records(state = "Bahia",
                                endemism = TRUE,
                                taxonomicStatus = "NOME_ACEITO")
```

## Filter by origin (native or introduced)

```r
bahia_introduced <- funga_records(state = "Bahia",
                                  establishmentMeans = "introduced")
```

## Filter by phytogeographic domain and nutritional mode

```r
caatinga_lichens <- funga_records(phytogeographicDomain = "Caatinga",
                                  lifeForm = "Liquenizado")
```

## Filter by substrate/host

```r
root_associates <- funga_records(habitat = "Planta viva - raiz")
```

## Save the result to a CSV file

```r
funga_records(taxon = "Trichoderma",
             save = TRUE,
             dir = "funga_records",
             filename = "trichoderma_records")
```

## Additional Tips

- `taxon` is matched against the `family`, `genus` and `taxonName` columns automatically — a family name ending in `"aceae"`, a single-word genus, or a multi-word species name are all detected and matched appropriately.
- Combine multiple filters freely: they are always ANDed together, so `funga_records(taxon = "Hymenochaetaceae", state = "Bahia", endemism = TRUE)` returns Hymenochaetaceae species endemic to Bahia (found only there — see [Endemism](#endemism) above if you instead want every Brazilian endemic occurring in Bahia).
- If you already have your own species list to resolve rather than browse the checklist by criteria, use [`funga_search()` or `funga_match()`](/articles/resolve_species_names.qmd) instead.
